## Critique
- claim-1: This correctly identifies the evidentiary deficiency, consistent with the accepted task-70 finding, but it does not establish the requested certificate. The five degree-\(d+3\) cases do not determine fifteen unidentified cases. No exact conditions, column orders, selected-row indices, matrices, or entrywise products are supplied, so the strategy reaches none of the certificate’s substantive acceptance criteria.

## Repair certificates
- [source-refresh] Provide the complete table (4) from `research-attempt-research-plan-task-68-1`, with a stable locator, containing all fifteen case conditions, ordered available columns, selected-row convention, and intended \(R_{\mathrm{full}}\).
- [proof-attempt] For each of those fifteen disjoint and exhaustive cases, explicitly derive \(R_{\mathrm{selected}}\) and an integral \(\mathcal C\), then display \(R_{\mathrm{full}}\) and verify every entry of \(\mathcal C R_{\mathrm{selected}}=R_{\mathrm{full}}\).
- [computation] Supply an independently executable exact-integer witness encoding all fifteen triples \((R_{\mathrm{selected}},\mathcal C,R_{\mathrm{full}})\), checking dimensions, integrality, case count, and every matrix equality, with captured output and exit status.

## Required revisions
- Replace the non-establishment report with the complete fifteen-case certificate once the missing table is available.
- Do not infer any of the absent ten cases from the accepted five-case degree-\(d+3\) certificate.
- Conclude only whether this matrix certificate is established; make no parent-theorem claim.
